images.seen: with Cliopatria: Zhou dynasty as one block with the small fengjian states (Wu, Lai, Ju, Xing, Pi...) winning their land by the size rule; Chu, Qin, Jin, Shu, Van Lang placed; looks right as drawn
Zhou dissolved: Jin, Qi, Lu, Qin take its land, 1115 cells left unowned; Lai, Ji, Tan, Sui still drawn; Quanrong in the Wei valley with Qin hatched contest
with Cliopatria: Qi has swallowed Lai, Ji, Tan and Sui (no Lai row in Cliopatria, so its Qi shape holds their land) - wrong, patched; Qin, Wu, Chu are deliberately smaller than Cliopatria's

Egypt: 25th Dynasty (dark brown) holds the Nile strip and Delta, Kingdom of Kush (light brown) the Nubian blob and the Western Desert; a 524-cell Kushite exclave in Matruh from -711 was wrong, patched

with Cliopatria: Near East right in layout (22nd Dynasty Lower Egypt, 23rd Upper Egypt corrected from Cliopatria's swapped labels; Assyria with vassal tints, Neo-Hittite and Aramaean states, Qedar, Urartu, Phrygia, Tabal); nothing needing a patch
after-patch stage: Lai, Ji (Shandong), Tan and Sui drawn as their own states inside Qi's Cliopatria shape; Qi smaller but coherent

issues.what: Greek city-states' -720 gain 'the Achaean colonies of the Ionian coast of Italy' resolves the whole region Magna Graecia (Calabria, Apulia, Basilicata, Campania and all Sicily): 279 cells drawn to the aggregate for 11 years, dropped by the -709 keyframe (281-cell snap). Sybaris, Croton and Taras have their own dossiers; the page has coastal foundations only.

Kingdom of Kush's -711 gain 'the Saite Delta' names the region Lower Egypt, which the gazetteer builds with the whole Matruh governorate, and its counterpart is a name rather than a slug, so it took 509 unowned desert cells (about 129,000 km2) as a detached exclave 1,000 km from Nubia. The Delta is already the 25th Dynasty's from -712; Cliopatria's Kush shape holds only 15 Matruh cells.

Qi keyframe qi_-750 (Cliopatria's Qi shape, 'ok') contains the land of Lai, Ji (Shandong), Tan and Sui, which have no Cliopatria rows; rule R2 handed Qi 124 cells at -750, so the four states vanished 183 to 18 years before Qi annexed them (Ji 690, Tan 684, Sui 681, Lai 567). Packet snap qi_-750 (124 added) and the lai/qi, ji-shandong/qi, qi/tan, qi/sui-ningyang conflicts.

Kingdom of Kush and twenty-fifth-dynasty-of-egypt model the same Kushite conquest twice with different dates and reach (Kush ledger: Upper Egypt -754, Lower Egypt -727, Delta -711; 25th: Elephantine -754, Upper Egypt to Herakleopolis -728, whole valley -712). Kush draws 86 Delta cells at -720 and 13-18 Middle Egypt cells at -750 as direct land, 15 to 18 years before the 25th does, and R2 settles 213 cell-years between them. No patch cancels a dossier's own events.

Jin keyframe jin_-750 (136,796 km2 for -750..-551) is far larger than the page's divided Jin of 746-678 (Quwo branch); the dossier itself marks the extent unverified. Jin also takes Western Guo (26 cells) and Yu (4) at -750, years before 655, because those states have no Cliopatria rows.
Phrygia keyframe phrygia_-750 adds 176 cells in Kastamonu, Bolu and Cankiri (Paphlagonia) as a snap; the dossier calls the shape ok but unverified (no page gives a Phrygian border).

Size-rule conflicts of the Zhou dynasty at -800 (wu 104, lai 98, ju 53, xing 27, pi 27, liu-lu-an 24...) and the other small-state wins (ba/chu -703 139 cells, a 100 km disc at Yichang; jin/xing, ju/lu, pi/xu): the smaller state rightly wins.

Assyria's -800 snap (151 cells) takes 52 of Van province's 80 cells from Urartu (Cliopatria's Assyria shape holds them to -701) and Urartu's -800/-750 snaps (183 and 11 cells); Babylonia drawn empty -728..-722 and from -710 (dossier: ruled directly by the Assyrian king); Qin/Yiqu R2 at -720 (Qin keeps 103 cells inside the Yiqu land); 22nd Dynasty -380 snap at -800 (seam between its -837 and -800 keyframes); Qedar 417-cell status changes at -738 and -716.
Eastern Zhou is drawn with 45 cells at -751, a year before its dossier starts (-750), because zhou-dynasty's dissolve event (-751) names it as successor.

dossier_requests.what: Drop or re-date the Egyptian gains of its ledger (-754 Upper Egypt, -727 Lower Egypt, -711 Saite Delta) and keep Nubia only, or make twenty-fifth-dynasty-of-egypt its constituent; both dossiers draw the Kushite conquest of Egypt with different dates
dossier_requests.why: The 25th Dynasty dossier already dates Elephantine -754, Upper Egypt -728 and the whole valley -712 (page: Shebitku 'conquered the entire Nile Valley ... around 712 BC'); the Kush ledger puts Kush directly in the Delta from -727 and gives it an unowned Western Desert exclave from -711 (that exclave is patched)

problems: hierarchy: no row for twenty-fifth-dynasty-of-egypt under kingdom-of-kush, -754..-656, constituent: the 25th Dynasty is the Kushite dynasty of Egypt ('Kushite power stretched from the Mediterranean Sea to the present Ethiopian boundary'); a row would draw it at half tint of Kush and settle the double model; page https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twenty-fifth_Dynasty_of_Egypt

boundary: keyframe_overrides/0 (qi_-750) acts for -750..-551, so it reaches into m0700-m0601 and later windows; it only removes Lai, Ji, Tan and Sui land until their ledgers give it to Qi (690, 684, 681, 567) and Qi's -550 keyframe takes over. events/1 (Kush loss at -711) is permanent from -711 into the next window.

boundary: data/patches/m0700-m0601.json keyframe_overrides/0 (wu_-750, valid -750..-585) reaches into this window and in my trial creates a new snap wu_-750 at -750 (added 26, removed 57: Wu's Jiangsu component of 56 cells becomes unowned); not my entry, not changed.

Counterpart given as a name, not a slug ('Twenty-fourth Dynasty of Egypt (Sais)' in kingdom-of-kush ledger/3) makes a named-counterpart gain act on unowned land too; other dossiers with a name in counterpart may do the same.

gazetteer: the region 'Lower Egypt' contains the whole Matruh governorate (524 cells) and 'Nile Valley (Egypt)' the whole Matruh, New Valley, Red Sea and both Sinai governorates, so any gain by these names draws Western Desert land; region 'Magna Graecia' includes all Sicily (89 cells of its 295).
Jin: the keyframe jin_-750..-551 is far larger than the divided Jin of 746-678 and no page opened gives an extent, so it is left (dossier notes ask for a gap-filler on the Jin annexation pages).
